Alright. [i]Buckshot Roulette[/i] is, well, a bit off center, and you've got to be a bit disturbed to enjoy this game. [b]I enjoyed this game a lot.[/b] :)

It's a very simple premise. You are meeting up with what seems to be a demonic host (whose name is apparently Josh. LMAO) in a nightclub to play some Russian Roulette....with a shotgun, and an alternate set of rules. Winner takes all...the cash. The cash being actually meaningless outside of being the basis for the game's leaderboard (of which there is one), but at least you know you're leaving with something, lol. You begin in a disgusting bathroom, walk onto a walkway overlooking a grimy dance club, and finally enter the game room itself, which is equally dank and disturbing. You sign a waiver (lol) and the match begins.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3276958087

In this version of Russian Roulette, you can choose to shoot yourself or the host. You just have to decide if you believe the next shell is a blank or not. Each of you begins with a random but equal amount of health. One live round equals one health point. After taking a shot, you are defibrillated back into the action until your health is completely gone, after which you wake up in a grimy bathroom to start the process over. If you win, you begin the next round. Each match features three rounds. Additionally, you can unlock a 'double or nothing' phase, wherein after winning, you can choose to take your winnings or try your luck again for double the cash (points). And you can continue to decide to double or nothing until you eventually lose or cash out. Double or Nothing is engaged at the beginning of the game once unlocked by taking 'QuayLudes' btw.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3276958064

Each round features the shotgun with a randomly determined amount of live and blank shells which are revealed before the shotgun is loaded by the host. Neither of you know which order the shells are loaded. You are then given an also randomly determined amount of items which you can use on your turn to boost damage, heal, remove shells, determine which shell is next, and so on. You have eight slots that can be filled with items, and the RNG selection of items happens every time the shotgun needs to be reloaded (and each reload goes through the same random shell reveal process). You might get to grab two items, you might get to grab six items. Who knows? You and the host each get the same number of selections. Each item has two quick animations enabled for them. One is your animation, one is Josh's animation.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3276957977

Your only real objective is to survive, and to advance up the leaderboard, while also of course knocking out some achievements. If you are a disturbed individual, this is the game for you, lol. It definitely earns the $2.99 price tag, and I'd say this fits nicely into the presentation of horror you might expect from a Dread Collection or Szymanski-verse or some such.

Buckshot Roulette is a highly stylised little experience. It likely won't occupy much of your time, but its singleplayer mode has atmosphere in spades, putting you in the dirty bathroom above a nightclub booming with music. You break through the doors to a little side space, a place that looks like you've made a wrong turn and just can't back out of. But you came here willingly.
A monster, blackened eyes and a great deal of teeth filling his misshapen mouth, has you sign a waiver, forfeiting your life if you lose the game. You're just here to win some cash.

The rules are simple. Random numbers of blanks and live rounds are fed into the shotgun in an equally random order. The dealer hands the gun to you, your turn. You gamble your life away, and win the first round.
Then more complexities are added. Items you can use to pierce the little mystery for just a moment. See what's currently in the chamber, take two turns in a row, double the damage. You only get a few of these per round, so make them count, take your chances when they come.
Of course, you can choose to shoot yourself. If it's blank, you get another turn. You just have to look down the barrel and pull the trigger.

This little back and forth goes on until you either lose and get yourself back together in that same bathroom, or win the cash and go home with a little victory music to go with it. That's it.

But now there's multiplayer! My friends and I hop on this sometimes if we need something settled that is simple to understand, has a bit of a skill ceiling to work upwards through, and that one person doesn't obviously trounce the other in. Currently, using this as a way for my DnD players to gamble their gold pieces away. It supports up to 4 players and is quite the cheap game. Pick it up, it deserves every cent and every bit of praise.

[h1] 7.5/10 [/h1]

Russian Roulette, well known for its high tension and thrill, has been extremely popular among many films and games, but there has never been a phenomenal game that has it as the theme until Buckshot Roulette came out. This game not only upgrades your weapon from a revolver to a much more powerful Remington 870 Model shotgun, but it also introduces some changes to traditional Russian Roulette. With simple and easy-to-grasp rules, fast-paced rounds and gameplay, and also, excellent performance effects for live-streaming, this little indie game has captured many players who come back to play it once again and again.

The art style of this work is very similar with the famous indie card game, Inscryption, but the overall feeling is much more gritty, and through the clever use of shadow and light, combined with the surprisingly excellent Techno style soundtrack, Buckshot Roulette has successfully created a yet utmost depressed, creepy, and also excited atmosphere. One thing different from traditional Russian Roulette is that you could point your gun towards the opponents, allowing you to flexibly transform from passive to positive. Also, the addition of items makes the gamble no more a pure game of luck and probability, how to plan your strategy is the key to victory. Also, the AI of the dealer is much smarter, adding a few more challenges to the player's single-player game experience.

Did Buckshot Roulette make the most use of its potential? Well, from my experience, definitely not. After every load, the player is always the first to go, this design makes the gameplay lacks randomness. There are always too many items for you in each load, so making each win much more based on the Item's order and best choices, somewhat making the game feel like a solely puzzle game to make the optimal choice, diminishes the tension and excitement brought by the uncertainty of traditional Russian Roulette. For now, the gameplay shown by it is too limited, in addition to the highly repetitive and homogeneous game experience, the cash you earn in the game is just a number and has no practical use, this could easily make most players feel bored after several tries.

The short-term popularity of Buckshot Roulette actually told us, that if you could make a game's gameplay extremely easy to understand and grasp, also it is eye-catching and has a very good live broadcast effect, it could succeed. But there is always a huge gap between watching others play a game and playing it yourself. If you want to give it a try because of its recent popularity, consider whether the repetitive gameplay could truly keep you after several tries. There is no doubt that the quality and potential of Buckshot Roulette suit its prices, but if the Officials could not release the multiplayer modes and enrich the single player contents in time, the current craze it is showing might just be a flash in the pan.

I first heard of Buckshot Roulette when it was having its moment, and while the concept drew me in, I never got around to it until recently. two years late and a 100k reviews deep, but here’s my two cents anyway, for whatever they’re worth from someone with the benefit of hindsight.

this is a practically perfect $3 game with an indescribable level of polish. the premise is simple: russian roulette with an array of items that let you manipulate the odds. you play against the dealer, a creepy masked entity, until you win. once you do, you can keep pushing for double or nothing till oblivion. the gameplay loop is so tight and addictive that I’ve sunk 12 hours into the same thing over and over and I’m still willing to do more. that’s the whole pitch, really. it earns every minute of it.

the multiplayer mode matches the original, maybe surpasses it. where the base game is about reading a system, multiplayer is about reading people. there’s a particular rush that comes from taking a stupid risk against a real opponent and watching it land. the stakes feel higher because they are.

normally, I’d factor in sale prices, but this game’s $3. if anything here appealed to you, there’s genuinely no reason not to play it. wholehearted recommend.

Game:

Is basically Russian roulette, but with extra lives and a bunch of artifacts that change how each round plays out. You can play solo against an AI or with friends, and every match feels tense and unpredictable thanks to the added mechanics.

Personal Opinion:

Whether you’re playing solo or with friends, the game is surprisingly fun and entertaining. Winning is mostly about luck, but you also have to actually use your brain— because if you don’t use your head correctly, you’ll literally lose it. Making smart use of whatever artifacts you’re given is what separates a win from an instant game over. When things go your way, it feels great; when they don’t, it’s usually hilarious. The simplicity mixed with constant tension makes it way more engaging than it sounds on paper.

Technical Stuff:

The game is built on the Godot engine, which uses the Vulkan API instead of DirectX. This can be an issue for some users, especially on macOS. The simplest workaround is using a Windows virtual machine.

Some players also report the game not launching or throwing errors. In most cases, the fix is just updating to the latest Vulkan graphics drivers. If you run into any other issues, the Steam Community is very active and almost always has an answer.

Completion Notes:

Most people will probably buy this game to play with friends, but keep in mind that achievements can only be unlocked in solo mode — multiplayer doesn’t count. Personally, this wasn’t a problem since the AI is actually pretty solid.

Some achievements require a bit of grinding, while others are very easy. Overall, you can get the Perfect in under 10 hours without too much trouble.

Buckshot Roulette is an interesting game with a great atmosphere and visuals. 
The game is VERY luck/RNG based on multiple levels:

1. Which order the shells are in 
2. What items you get 
3. What items the dealer gets

But there is still some strategy to it. You have to think about which items to use in what order or which ones ones to steal if you get the adrenaline shot (that item lets you steal and use one item from the dealer). Now, you can play perfectly and still get absolutely forked by the dealer. It is a gambling game after all.

There is the normal mode, which is pretty easy to beat and a "double or nothing" mode which poses a challenge with more items. The achievements are fine, but 2-3 are insanely difficult and will be very annoying (especially if you play optimally and still lose). If you like the game, you can expect 3-10 hours of playtime, which is fair for the price. There is not a lot of content, so be aware of that. If you just play the main mode and some endless mode, your experience will be pretty short. If you want to get all achievements and play some multiplayer, your playtime will be a lot longer.

Buckshot Roulette is a short dark Russian roulette game that aims to try to mess up with your opponent as much as possible while pushing your luck to the limit to win rounds in the most obnoxious way possible. The game is easy to learn and captivates the player's attention with the raw emotion of...gambling. Yeah, that's right! Gambling! But we gamble our lives, with shotgun shells. 

Having one real round in the chamber with two fake ones makes one heart pound when you go for that risky "I am gonna believe this round is real" and you shoot the dealer only to see that it was indeed a real bullet, giving huge satisfaction when making high-risk play. I like the items in the game as they add a "try to read your opponent's next move" layer to it and the possibility to create combos. The goal is to try to set up each turn and round maximizing your damage while reducing your opponent's moves.

The only thing the game is lacking is multiplayer, which it needs BADLY because this is such an amazing little game that could get a lot of replayability when facing human foes. A single run can last from 30 minutes to 1 hour and the Double or Nothing mode adds a lot of new items to the mix with more challenging gameplay, so there is still some replayability even when it is only single-player. For 2,99 you cannot go wrong with this game that is bound to entertain you for a while!

Note: In the future, the dev might add multiplayer!

Buckshot Roulette is one of those games that somehow turns a few simple mechanics into an incredibly tense experience — borderline psychological warfare.

Each round forces you to make decisions with limited information. Managing items, tracking shells, and deciding whether to take a risk or play it safe creates a constant sense of tension. Even when the odds seem to be in your favour, the game always finds a way to keep you on edge.

While strategy plays a major role in determining the outcome, luck has a heavy influence on every match. Sometimes everything falls into place, and other times you're left wondering what exactly you did to deserve the shell currently heading in your direction.

In terms of achievements, there is plenty to work towards. Most of them are fairly straightforward, and you'll unlock them naturally through normal play. The ones tied to Double or Nothing can require careful planning and are heavily influenced by luck.

They will most likely leave you lying awake at 4 AM, desperately trying to remember how many live rounds and blanks were loaded into the shotgun.

Buckshot Roulette is simple, tense, and surprisingly addictive. It doesn't take long to understand, but every round feels different enough to keep you coming back for one more game.
